description.value: This study investigated the effects of partial sleep restriction on emotional regulation through cognitive reappraisal in healthy younger and older adults using fMRI, including brain activity and amygdala connectivity.

spans.text: This study investigated the effects of sleep restriction on emotional regulation through cognitive reappraisal in older and younger participants.

value: We specifically hypothesized that sleep restriction would lead to decreased self-rated success in emotional regulation in response to negative stimuli, and that this effect would be associated with decreased activation of dlPFC and lOFC, increased amygdala activation and decreased connectivity between dlPFC/lOFC and amygdala .

description.value: Participants viewed negative and neutral pictures and were instructed to maintain, upregulate, or downregulate their emotional response, followed by ratings of task success.

spans.text: Each session consisted of 60 trials (15 maintain neutral, 15 maintain negative, 15 upregulate negative and 15 downregulate negative) ( figure 2 ).
Each session consisted of 60 trials
During fMRI, stimuli were shown using Presentation software (Neurobehavioral systems) displayed via fMRI-compatible goggles with an eye-tracker on the right eye (Arrington Research).

instructions.value: Following an arrow pointing upwards, participants were instructed to increase their emotional response; following an arrow pointing downwards, to decrease their emotional response; and following an arrow pointing to the right, to just look and not change their spontaneous reaction.

spans.text: Following an arrow pointing upwards, participants were instructed to increase their emotional response to the following stimulus. After an arrow pointing downwards, they were instructed to decrease their emotional response. Lastly, following an arrow pointing to the right, they were instructed to just look and not change their spontaneous reaction (maintain).
